title: Who Will Bow and Bend
description: A Shaker song in three strains from Mary Hazzard's songbook (about 1847): who will bow and bend like a willow, who will turn and twist and reel. Each strain is sung twice, as the book marks it. For 2 to 4 singers: the soprano sings the tune, the alto and tenor sing the words close beneath it, and the bass holds the roots on "oo".

licence.source: melody and words from Mary Hazzard's manuscript book "A Collection of Extra Songs of Various Kinds Written and Pricked For the Purpose of Retaining them" (begun February 7th 1847), Winterthur Library, ASC 893, catalogue https://winterthur.libraryhost.com/repositories/2/archival_objects/95, page images 38 and 39 (the manuscript's pages 18 and 19), with no heading (its first line "Who will bow and bend like a willow") and no place, giver or date, among songs of early 1847 (two songs away on each side, on pages 17 and 20, songs signed "Second Family Caterbury Feb 22nd 1847" (sic) and "Second Family Canterbury. April 1847."); in Shaker letteral notation in C in 2/4 (head frame "3" with the crossed double bar), sung here in C in 4/4 with every value doubled; every pitch as written; three strains, each sung twice, as the repeat signs mark them; breaths written in for beginners: "reel" gives up its second beat, and "dom," "ing," "er," "ting," "ing.", "it," and "ening." before its repeat end half a beat early, the line after each ("From", "Who", "Pride", "Mother's", "O", "I'll", and "Who" at the first strain's repeat) coming in half a beat late; spelling modernised: "real" sung "reel", "Mothers" written "Mother's", "&" sung "and"; "bower" sung in one syllable and "union" in two, as the notes give them; "gale" read for a word that could also be "gate"; read from the scan of the whole book saved by Hillel from the Winterthur Library. Courtesy Winterthur Museum, Garden & Library.
